reconcile.connective: JFB explain the Ezra–Nehemiah numeric gaps by the different times and places the two registers were drawn up, plus ordinary attrition over the intervening years.

discrepancy.connective: McKinsey's Encyclopedia of Biblical Errancy counts the Ezra–Nehemiah return registers among the Bible's numerical errors, noting that more than half of roughly thirty-five matched clan totals disagree — Bebai's 5-person gap among them.

skeptic.name: C. Dennis McKinsey
skeptic.attribution: C. Dennis McKinsey, The Encyclopedia of Biblical Errancy (Prometheus Books, 1995)

excerpts.excerpt_text: But the discrepancy is sufficiently accounted for from the different circumstances in which the two registers were taken; that of Ezra having been made up at Babylon, while that of Nehemiah was drawn out in Judea, after the walls of Jerusalem had been rebuilt. The lapse of so many years might well be expected to make a difference appear in the catalogue, through death or other causes; in particular, one person being, according to Jewish custom, called by different names.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Explicitly labels the Ezra 2 vs. Nehemiah 7 numeric variance 'the discrepancy' and gives the standard harmonization (different time/place of registration, attrition) that covers the Bebai gap.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on Ezra 2:3 (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Haley's specific-passage coverage of this pair could not be confirmed, so the row's own harmonizing commentator is used instead: K&D set the two registers side by side, clan by clan (Bebai's 623 vs. 628 included), and attribute the variance to copying rather than to two conflicting underlying facts.
